ui_bugs.issue: Progress bar is misleading: for rank #63 with nextBoundary=50 the bar renders width 98.6316% (measured on '.h-full.bg-amber-500' inline style), i.e. visually 'basically there' while the copy says 13 ranks still to go. Cause: `const prevBoundary = [...boundaries].reverse().find(b => b > rank)` returns the LARGEST boundary above the rank (1000) instead of the nearest one (100). span=950, done=937 -> 98.6%. With the nearest boundary it should be (100-63)/(100-50)=74%. Fix: `const prevBoundary = boundaries.find(b => b > rank) || rank + 100;` (ascending find is correct for the upper bound).

rca_of_the_issue: Milestone progress bar: computeNextMilestone derives the lower edge of the progress span with `[...boundaries].reverse().find(b => b > rank)`. Reversing makes find() return the first (i.e. largest) boundary greater than the rank, so for rank 63 it picks 1000 rather than 100, inflating the completed fraction to 937/950 = 98.6%. Repro: login as demo player, read the Next Milestone card bar width. Mitigation: use ascending `boundaries.find(b => b > rank)`.
